ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་རིགས་ཅན་གྱི་དབང་དུ་མཛད་ནས་འཕགས་པའི་གང་ཟག་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་སྨོས་ཏེ། བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་ནི་འཁོར་ལོས་སྒྱུར་བའི་བུ་ཕལ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོར་གྱུར་པ་བཞིན་དུ་ཉན་ཐོས་གཅིག་ཏུ་དཀའ་#བཞིན་དུ་བྱེད་པས་རྟོག་#པ་ཐོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་
པོ་ལྟ་བུར་གྱུར་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །འཇུག་པའི་གནས་སྐབས་ཀྱི་བྱེ་བྲག་ནི་རིགས་གསུམ་ཅར་ལ་ཡང་སྲིད་པས་དེའི་ཕྱིར་དེའི་དབང་དུ་མཛད་ནས་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་དུ་འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་དེད་དཔོན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་སྨོས་ཏེ། བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་ནི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་དུ་འཇུག་པ་
ཐར་པའི་ས་བོན་མ་སྐྱེས་པ་དེ་དག་གི་རིགས་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་དུ་ལམ་ནས་ལམ་གཞན་དུ་ཁྲིད་པར་མཛད་པའི་ཕྱིར་དེད་དཔོན་ཞེས་བྱའོ། །ཡེ་ཤེས་དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ། སྤོབས་པ་བསམ་གྱིས་མི་ཁྱབ་པ། གསུང་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ། དབྱངས་སྙན་པ། སྐུ་བྱད་བལྟ་བས་ཆོག་མི་ཤེས་པ། 
སྐུ་མཚུངས་པ་མེད་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་ཚིག་འདི་དྲུག་གིས་ནི་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་ཐབས་གང་གིས་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་#དོན་མཛད་པའི་ཐབས་དེ་སྟོན་ཏེ། ཐབས་དེ་ཡང་དེ་ལས་གསུམ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་ལ་{གོ་རིམས་,གོ་རིམ་}བཞིན་དུ་ཚིག་དང་པོས་ནི་ཡིད་ཀྱི་ཕྲིན་#ལས་སྟོན་ཏོ། །གསུམ་གྱིས་ནི་གསུང་གི་ཕྲིན་#

གྱི་#དོན་མཛད་པའི་ཐབས་ཡིན་པར་ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་#སྟེ། ཡེ་ཤེས་ནི་དེ་དང་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྤྱོད་པའི་ཕྱིར་འདིར་ཐུགས་ཀྱི་ཕྲིན་#ལས་ཞེས་བཤད་དོ། །ཡུལ་དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པས་ཡེ་ཤེས་དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ་ཡིན་ལ། དེ་དང་ལྡན་པས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཡེ་ཤེས་དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་སྟེ། སྐུ་དང་གསུང་གི་

truly entrusts the wheel to a son of the Universal Monarch who possesses the marks and becomes the father of those who know, the Blessed One is the "father of those."

Regarding the Hearer-lineage, it says "king of noble individuals." Just as a Universal Monarch becomes the king of his ordinary sons, the Blessed One is like a king to those who have attained realization through the difficult practice of the Hearers.

The distinction of the stage of entering applies to all three lineages while they are in existence. Therefore, regarding that, it says "caravan leader for those traveling to the city of Nirvana." The Blessed One is called a "caravan leader" because he leads those in whom the seed of liberation has not yet arisen into the city of Nirvana, guiding them from one path to another according to their respective lineages.

"Infinite wisdom; inconceivable eloquence; pure speech; melodious voice; a physical presence that one can never look at enough; a peerless body" — these six phrases show the methods by which the Blessed One performs the welfare of beings. Those methods are three. 

In sequence: the first phrase shows the activity of the mind. Three phrases show the activity of speech. Two phrases show the activity of the body. Because the activities of speech and body are the nature of teaching the Dharma and so forth, they are shown as the primary methods for performing the welfare of beings. The activity of the mind is also included as a method for performing the welfare of beings because it instigates all of them. Wisdom is explained here as "mental activity" because it operates together with the mind. Because its objects are infinite, his wisdom is infinite; and possessing that, the Blessed One is called "Infinite Wisdom." The characteristics of the activities of body and speech are held to be the methods for performing the welfare of beings; they are also infinite, and the Tathagata's wisdom engages with them without obstruction. 

The activity of speech shows the specific perfections of the qualities of eloquence and pure melody. In that regard,

tail: the specific quality of eloquence is also of two kinds: that based on the letter and that based on the meaning.
old_translation:
Regarding those of the Hearer-lineage, it is said he is the "King of Noble Persons." Just as the Universal Monarch becomes the king of his ordinary sons, the Blessed One is like a king to those who have attained realization while practicing the difficult path of a Hearer. 
Regarding the specific state of entering, it applies to all three lineages. For that purpose, it is said he is the "Caravan leader of those traveling to the city of Nirvana." 
The Blessed One is called "Caravan leader" because he leads those who have not yet produced the seeds of liberation toward the city of Nirvana, guiding them from one path to another according to their respective lineages. 
"Immeasurable wisdom," "Inconceivable eloquence," "Pure speech," "Melodious voice," "Body that one can never tire of beholding," 
"Incomparable body"—these six phrases show the methods by which the Blessed One performs the benefit of beings. These methods are threefold. 
Respectively, the first phrase shows the activity of the mind. Three phrases show the activity of speech. 
Two phrases show the activity of the body. Since the activities of speech and body are in the nature of showing the teaching of the Dharma and so forth, they are shown to be the primary methods for benefiting beings. 
The activity of the mind is also included as a method for benefiting beings because it motivates all the others. 
Wisdom is said here to be the "activity of the mind" because it functions together with it. 
His wisdom is immeasurable because its objects are immeasurable; possessing that, the Blessed One is said to have "immeasurable wisdom." 
The characteristics of the activities of body and speech are the methods for benefiting beings; they too are immeasurable and the Blessed One's wisdom engages with them without obstruction.
